<a id="acceptance-criteria-11"></a>

### Acceptance criteria

1. `book new` creates a book under the configured docs root, registers it, and renders its README in
   the default monolith mode.
2. A book created outside the docs root is either refused or explicitly allowed by a named flag;
   there is no silent third location.
3. The library README renders at the project root, carries `[Document Index]` navigation at the top
   and bottom, and contains the Document Index of all registered books in registry order.
4. Library defaults apply to a book that has no explicit value; a per-book value wins.
5. Library sync renders every registered book and reports per-book drift without writing under
   `--check`.
6. Moving or renaming a registered book updates the registry and its output path and leaves its
   container and bodies unchanged; both are refused while the book is open, as is unregister.
7. No command in the new tool opens, lists or modifies a legacy container (integration test with a
   fake legacy directory proves it is ignored).
8. The cut-over milestone passes: `pecia sync --check` is clean on the CLABOK repository, the README
   is generated (not hand-edited), and a change to a body renders through `sync --write`.
9. `library` has no command that imports or adopts an existing book.


<a id="design-decisions-for-this-scope-s-planning-session-11"></a>

### Design decisions for this scope's planning session

- Registry schema and its version, and the migration/refusal policy for an older registry.
- Where the library's own policy fields live (registry entry versus a separate library manifest).
- Book ID derivation (slug, sequence) and how it relates to the output path; renaming a book versus
  renaming its folder.
- The exact `book new` flag set for the opt-ins (numbering, toc, index depth, output mode) and which
  of them are library defaults versus per-book overrides.
- Whether `Docs/<slug>` is one folder per book with generated files directly, or a subfolder per mode.
- What the scaffold README keeps (checks section, release note) and whether those become blocks of the
  library book.
- Whether unregister deletes anything (default: nothing) and what it does with an orphaned output
  folder.
- Whether the Document Index is generated from the registry or from the layout block sources, and how
  the two are kept consistent.


<a id="risks-and-constraints-11"></a>

### Risks and constraints

- The hard cut is the core risk control of this plan. Do not add an import path "just in case"; it
  reopens migration complexity.
- The README is the project's front page. Treat the cut-over as a deliberate content migration of the
  scaffold text, not as an automatic conversion of the old DocEngine library.
- Library defaults plus per-book values form a two-level configuration. Test the precedence, because
  the failure is silent (a book renders with the wrong mode).
- An open book must not move. The registry update and the file move are two steps; the guard belongs
  before either.


<a id="s12-editorial-state-and-generated-content"></a>

## S12 — Editorial State and Generated Content ![status: Final](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-Final-brightgreen?style=flat-square)

Status: in progress (S12a delivered 2026-11-05; S12b–S12e open).
Phase: 7. Depends on: S09 (render placement contract). Blocks: none, but S11 is its first consumer.
PLAN refs: §3.14 (regions, footer, notes, index prose, status, badges, layout block), §3 (4),
§3.11 (asciiui types are an S09 concern).


<a id="current-state-and-pre-planned-decisions-2026-11-05-2"></a>

### Current state and pre-planned decisions (2026-11-05)

- Regions already exist in the model (`Region{ID, Kind, Target, Blocks}`; footer/notes) and the
  renderer renders them (`footer`, `notesFor`) at their target. Authoring commands are missing.
- `internal/asciiui` exists: `Parse`, `Render(spec, overrides)`, `Defaults`, `Resolve`. The renderer
  reads `<book>/layouts/asciiui/<blockID>.asciiui` and reports `render.missing-layout` when absent.
- `structure.AddLockedBlock(book, parent, "UILayout")` creates the locked anchor block; the body and
  type commands reject locked blocks, while moves and removals stay allowed.
- Index prose is not modelled; `render`'s `entry`/`indexMarkdown` is the render hook.
- Status, badges and the layout block do not exist.

Pre-planned decisions:

- Manifest v3 adds one-line index prose per node (`prose`) and any status fields; one version bump
  covers all S12 model additions.
- ASCII UI commands: `asciiui add --book <id> --parent <node> --file <spec>`,
  `asciiui set --book <id> --block <id> --file <spec>`, `asciiui remove --book <id> --block <id>`
  (delete the spec, then `remove` the locked block). The spec path is fixed, not configurable.
- Region commands: `region set --book <id> --kind footer --file <path|->`,
  `region notes --book <id> --target <node|block> --file <path|->`,
  `region remove --book <id> --target <node|block>`; the footer slot is one per book.
- Index prose renders after the entry title; it never enters the ToC.
- Status is opt-in per book, tool-owned vocabulary, rendered through the placement contract.
- Badges and the layout block stay last; the layout block is deferred and uses `git ls-files`.


<a id="goal-12"></a>

### Goal

Model authored content that is not part of the chapter flow — footer, notes and status — as blocks in
ordered collections, and generate the repository-derived content (badges, layout tree) from facts
instead of hand-written markup, while removing the header and preamble regions from the model.


<a id="in-scope-12"></a>

### In scope

| # | Requirement | PLAN |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Regions are blocks: a region is a block with a stable ID in an ordered collection; there are no separate region sources or region types; collection order is render order | §3.14 |
| 2 | Region collections have a stable ID and a target: a node, a block or the book | §3 (4), §3.14 |
| 3 | Footer: a region collection with exactly one slot per book; tool-owned, replaceable through a command, always rendered in the book's `README.md` at the bottom above the navigation | §3.14 |
| 4 | Notes: a region collection attached to a structural node or a block; rendered directly beneath the target, before the next element; placement tool-owned, text authored through a command | §3.14 |
| 5 | Header and preamble are not part of the model and have no code path | §3.14 |
| 6 | Status system: opt-in per book; the tool owns the vocabulary (states, assignments, legend, badges) and renders it structurally; authors never write the status markup | §3.14 |
| 7 | Badges: generated from repository facts; an explicit message overrides the detector; the generated badge region is never hand-edited | §3.14 |
| 8 | Layout block: opt-in, deferred from the first delivery; generated from `git ls-files`; without git it is a no-op, not an error; a command authors it from a path and a depth; endpoints and branches can be excluded afterwards; per-path prose is authored through commands; the generated tree is never hand-edited | §3.14 |
| 9 | Index prose: each index entry can carry optional prose, authored and stored here, rendered by S09 | §3.14 |
| 10 | Every authored change goes through a command with dry-run, rollback and open-book requirement | §6 |
| 11 | Removal of region content is a command; there is no hand editing of a generated file | §3.14 |


<a id="out-of-scope-13"></a>

### Out of scope

- Render placement mechanics, heading emission, index line format: S09.
- Grammar gate and term list: S13.
- Status or badge authoring on the rendering side beyond the placement contract: S09.
- Header, preamble and legacy residue cleanup: explicitly not carried over.
- Layout block as part of the first delivery: explicitly deferred by `PLAN.md` (this scope delivers
  it last, and can ship without it).


<a id="deliverables-12"></a>

### Deliverables

- `internal/model` extension for region collections where S03 did not already cover it (coordinate:
  S03 owns the type, this scope owns the semantics and commands).
- `internal/editorial` (or the responsible package): footer, notes, status, badges, layout, index
  prose authoring and storage.
- Commands for each region and for status assignment/legend and badge override.
- Badge detectors driven by repository facts (git remote, license, Go version, module path).
- Layout generator over `git ls-files` with depth, include/exclude and per-path prose.
- Tests: footer single-slot enforcement, note adjacency after a reorder, status legend golden, badge
  override precedence, layout with a fixture repository and without git, exclusion rules.
- This scope's implementation plan under `Planning/plans/`.


<a id="acceptance-criteria-12"></a>

### Acceptance criteria

1. A footer command replaces the single slot; a second footer is impossible; the footer renders in
   the README above the navigation in every output mode.
2. A note attached to a node renders directly beneath that node, before the next element, and follows
   the node after a reorder.
3. Removing a note removes exactly its block and leaves the rest of the collection order intact.
4. Status is opt-in: a book without status renders no legend and no status markup; an enabled book
   renders states, assignments and legend from tool-owned data.
5. An explicit badge message overrides the detector; a detector without a source omits the badge and
   reports it, and no badge line is hand-editable (a hand edit is not preserved by a render).
6. The layout block renders a deterministic tree from a fixture repository, honours depth and
   exclusions, and is a no-op without git.
7. `grep` over the code base finds no header or preamble region code path.
8. Index prose round-trips through its command and renders on its entry (contract test with S09).
9. Every change in this scope creates a rollback package and respects the open-book requirement.


<a id="design-decisions-for-this-scope-s-planning-session-12"></a>

### Design decisions for this scope's planning session

- Status vocabulary and its transitions (which states exist, whether they are configurable per book).
- Badge detector set and the repository facts each one reads; what "optional" means for a missing
  source (omit versus placeholder).
- Whether the layout block, explicitly deferred, is part of this scope at all or a separate follow-up
  scope. If it stays, plan it as the last milestone of S12.
- Note ordering when several notes target the same node, and whether a note can target a region.
- Footer command shape (set, clear, show) and whether the footer can contain multiple blocks (one slot
  can still hold an ordered list).
- Whether index prose is a field on the node or a separate block in a book-level collection.
- Where the generated marker for badges and layout lives, and how it interacts with S09's
  foreign-file protection.
- Whether status is rendered as inline markers, a trailing legend, or both, and the exact rendering
  belongs to S09's placement contract.


<a id="risks-and-constraints-12"></a>

### Risks and constraints

- Generated content must regenerate deterministically. A badge or layout block that depends on the
  environment (locale, time) breaks `sync --check`.
- `git ls-files` only lists tracked paths. Untracked files never appear; that is intended and must be
  documented in the tool output.
- The footer and notes are blocks. Do not introduce a second region storage next to the block pool;
  `PLAN.md` removed the separate region sources deliberately.
- Header and preamble must be gone, not deprecated. Grep for them in the acceptance test.


<a id="refinement-2026-11-05"></a>

### Refinement (2026-11-05)

- The ASCII UI layout feature does not get its own container type. It creates a block, sets its
  type to `UILayout` and locks it. The block is the render anchor: the drawing is inserted at its
  placement, and `locked` keeps the generated body out of manual edits. The primitive is
  `structure.Service.AddLockedBlock`.


<a id="s13-grammar-gate-and-term-list"></a>

## S13 — Grammar Gate and Term List ![status: Final](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-Final-brightgreen?style=flat-square)

Status: draft, not planned.
Phase: 7. Depends on: S02 (grammar endpoint), S08 (prose-writing commands, temp). Blocks: none.
PLAN refs: §3.14 (terms and grammar), §3.7 (LanguageTool daemon state stays in the OS temp
directory), §3.11 (grammar endpoint), §6 (grammar gate on prose writes, confirmation flow).


<a id="current-state-and-pre-planned-decisions-2026-11-05-3"></a>

### Current state and pre-planned decisions (2026-11-05)

- The single prose-write path is `body.Service.write` (lock, normalize, `prose.CheckProse`,
  `SnapshotBody`, `WriteAtomic`); the grammar gate hooks in before the snapshot.
- Body gate failures are rejects: `body.forbidden-heading`, `body.expectation-failed` through
  `body.MapError`.
- `config.Values.GrammarEndpoint` exists (default `""` = local LanguageTool default); there is no
  policy key yet.
- `store.Layout.Terms()` is `<store>/terms.txt`; no code writes it.
- The coordination daemon (`pecia serve`, AF_UNIX) is unrelated to the grammar server.
- `apply` has no body step today; if it gains one, the gate must cover it.

Pre-planned decisions:

- Add `grammar.policy` (`block` default, `warn`, `off`) to `clabok.json` with strict validation.
- Findings `{block, line, column, rule, message, replacements}`; the block policy returns a reject
  with the findings as details.
- Terms: requests create pending entries; `terms commit` requires explicit confirmation; the tool
  never writes `terms.txt` directly.
- Tests use a fake HTTP server; a missing Java/LanguageTool wrapper degrades to a warning, not a
  failure.
- The server lifecycle is opt-in; the default is the local server, and the state, lock and log live
  in the OS temp directory.


<a id="goal-13"></a>

### Goal

Gate prose writes with a grammar check whose policy is explicit, and make the term list a
tool-owned, confirmation-gated artifact so that no prose write and no term change happens silently.


<a id="in-scope-13"></a>

### In scope

| # | Requirement | PLAN |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | LanguageTool client: HTTP check over the configured endpoint (S02); default is the local daemon in the OS temp directory | §3.11, §3.14 |
| 2 | Findings model: block ID, line, column, rule, message, replacements; JSON by default | §3.10 |
| 3 | Gate policy on prose-writing commands: `block` (default, refuse a finding), `warn` (write and report), `off` (skip); a missing Java/wrapper/server degrades to a warning, never a hard failure | §3.14 |
| 4 | Applying selected findings: a batch replace with an expected count, atomic, one rollback package | §3.14, §6 |
| 5 | Term list: tool-owned and lives in the store; `set` and `delete` are requests that create a pending entry, never a write; commit requires explicit confirmation; `pending`, `discard` and batch commit exist | §3.14, §6 |
| 6 | Terms suppress invented names and domain compounds in findings; the term list never changes a body by itself | §3.14 |
| 7 | Server lifecycle: `serve` starts or attaches to the one shared server, `server-stop`, `server-info`; concurrent checks share one server; idle timeout is configurable | §3.11, §3.14 |
| 8 | Daemon state (state file, lock, log) stays in the OS temp directory and is never part of the store | §3.7 |
| 9 | The gate runs inside the body-write path defined by S08; it never writes by itself | §3.14 |
| 10 | Offline and failure behaviour is explicit and stable: an unreachable server yields a warning and the configured policy applies to a finding-free result | §3.14 |


<a id="out-of-scope-14"></a>

### Out of scope

- Body read/write and replace mechanics: S08 (this scope plugs into its write gate).
- The Unity editor grammar bridge: not carried over; CLABOK has no Unity editor.
- Terms UI beyond the commands: S14 may surface them, it does not own them.
- Grammar configuration keys beyond the endpoint: S02.
- Any change to docengine or its LanguageTool wrappers: read-only reference.


<a id="deliverables-13"></a>

### Deliverables

- `internal/grammar`: client, findings, policy enforcement, finding application, server lifecycle
  commands.
- `internal/grammar` terms store (or the owning package for `terms.txt` in the store): pending
  requests, confirmation, commit, discard, lookups.
- A fake server used by tests so the suite is offline and deterministic.
- Commands: grammar check (book, block, file or raw text), grammar apply, terms set/delete/pending/
  commit/discard/list.
- Tests: gate matrix (block/warn/off), server-absent matrix, apply atomicity, pending/commit flow,
  term suppression, concurrent checks sharing one server.
- This scope's implementation plan under `Planning/plans/`.


<a id="acceptance-criteria-13"></a>

### Acceptance criteria

1. With policy `block`, a prose write that produces a finding is refused and the body is unchanged;
   with `warn` it is written and the findings are reported on stderr/stdout per the output contract;
   with `off` no check runs.
2. With no server reachable, the configured policy still applies to a finding-free result and the
   command reports the degraded check exactly once (no repeated warnings per finding).
3. Applying selected findings changes only the chosen findings, atomically, with a rollback package.
4. `terms set` and `terms delete` never modify `terms.txt`; they return a pending ID and a reason.
5. `terms commit` without the explicit confirmation fails; with it, the term list is updated once and
   the pending entry is removed.
6. A pending entry survives a process restart and can be recovered.
7. A term suppresses its finding in a subsequent check; removing it restores the finding.
8. Two concurrent checks start or share exactly one server process; `server-info` reports it.
9. The OS temp directory holds the server state, lock and log; the store contains none of them.


<a id="design-decisions-for-this-scope-s-planning-session-13"></a>

### Design decisions for this scope's planning session

- Whether grammar is part of the first delivery at all, or a later opt-in module (it is not required
  for the M5 milestone).
- Finding identity: how a finding is addressed for `apply` (stable ID per run, or line/column/rule).
- Replacement policy: only unambiguous single-suggestion findings are auto-applied by default.
- Terms file format, case sensitivity, deduplication and the confirmation record (who, when, reason).
- Server start semantics: whether `serve` is required before a check in `daemon`-like setups or the
  check starts a short-lived local server; `PLAN.md` requires one shared server, not a specific
  start path.
- Timeouts and retry policy for slow servers, and whether a timeout blocks a write under `block` or
  degrades.
- Whether `grammar check --file`/`--text` (non-book prose) is in scope; it is useful for the tool's
  own documentation and cheap to add.
- How the gate interacts with `--dry-run` (no check, or check and report without writing).


<a id="risks-and-constraints-13"></a>

### Risks and constraints

- A grammar server is an external process. The test suite must not depend on a network or on Java;
  use a fake server and an explicit integration test that is skipped when unavailable.
- The gate must never become a reason a valid write is lost silently. `block` is a refusal with an
  error code, `warn` is a write with a report; there is no third, silent state.
- Term changes are the only path that modifies the suppression list. Direct file edits are a defect
  even if the format is plain text.


<a id="s14-terminal-ui"></a>

## S14 — Terminal UI ![status: Final](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-Final-brightgreen?style=flat-square)

Status: draft, not planned.
Phase: 8. Depends on: S07 (structure), S08 (body), S09 (render), plus S05/S06 behaviour at runtime.
Blocks: none.
PLAN refs: §3.10 (TUI included, one tooling surface), §3.13 (package responsibility), §3.11 (config).


<a id="current-state-and-pre-planned-decisions-2026-11-05-4"></a>

### Current state and pre-planned decisions (2026-11-05)

- The CLI surface is complete for authoring and rendering; every payload implements `Text()` and
  mutating receipts implement `DryRunResult()`.
- The core services are plain Go (`structure`, `body`, `render`, `lifecycle`, `search`, `temp`) and
  can be called in-process.
- The relevant rules are one static binary and no new dependency without an owner decision.

Pre-planned decisions:

- Entry `pecia tui`, only when stdin and stdout are a TTY; otherwise a clear error, never an
  interactive fallback in pipelines.
- No TUI library without an explicit owner decision; the default is a hand-rolled renderer over the
  existing services.
- Panes: structure tree, body editor/view (external editor or inline), status line, sync/check.
- Core errors surface as `cli.Error` codes; the TUI adds no domain rules.
- View models are tested without a terminal.


<a id="goal-14"></a>

### Goal

Give humans an interactive terminal surface on the same core services, without a second
implementation of any book behaviour and without making the CLI interactive.


<a id="in-scope-14"></a>

### In scope

| # | Requirement | PLAN |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | The TUI ships in the same static binary and uses the same core services; no domain logic in the UI package | §3.10 |
| 2 | The CLI remains the complete tooling surface; automation, agents and CI use the CLI, never the TUI | §3.10 |
| 3 | The TUI is the only interactive surface: no prompts in the CLI commands | §3.10 |
| 4 | Core operations reachable: open/close, structure navigation and editing, body editing, settings, sync/check, status | §3.10 |
| 5 | Behaviour under errors is the core's behaviour: stable error objects are shown, not re-implemented; locked or stale resources surface as a recoverable state | §3.12 |
| 6 | Deterministic, ASCII-only rendering; no dependency on terminal features beyond common ANSI capabilities; works in Windows Terminal and common Unix terminals | §3.10 |
| 7 | Editing a body either opens the external editor or uses an inline editor; the choice is a design decision, not a product statement | §3.10 |
| 8 | View models are testable without a terminal (input events -> state -> output lines) | §6 (test suite) |


<a id="out-of-scope-15"></a>

### Out of scope

- Any new capability that the CLI does not expose.
- GUI, web UI or remote UI.
- Replacing the CLI in CI or in agent workflows.
- The daemon's server mode: S06.
- Config semantics: S02.


<a id="deliverables-14"></a>

### Deliverables

- A TUI package with view models, input handling and a renderer over the core services.
- Wiring in `cmd/pecia` (a subcommand or a mode, decided in planning) that does not add logic to
  `main`.
- View-model tests: navigation, editing, error surface, lock conflict, no-terminal fallback.
- A short user-facing key map (authored with CLABOK once S11 has landed; a plain Markdown note
  before that).
- This scope's implementation plan under `Planning/plans/`.


<a id="acceptance-criteria-14"></a>

### Acceptance criteria

1. The TUI performs a full round-trip on a fixture book: create node, write body, move block, sync,
   close.
2. Every TUI action maps to an existing core operation; a parity test enumerates the actions and
   fails when one has no core call.
3. No domain rule (level limit, heading rule, block-ID rule) is implemented in the TUI package;
   violations surface as core errors.
4. A locked or stale resource produces a visible, recoverable state and no lost input.
5. The TUI runs without a terminal (piped output) by falling back to a plain mode or a clear error.
6. Package tests pass in CI without a TTY; `go test -race` remains clean.


<a id="design-decisions-for-this-scope-s-planning-session-14"></a>

### Design decisions for this scope's planning session

- TUI library: standard library only versus a dependency. `PLAN.md` requires one static binary, not a
  zero-dependency UI; a dependency is an owner decision (see `Planning/README.md` §8).
- Entry point: `pecia tui` versus a mode when both stdin and stdout are a TTY. The latter is
  convenient but must never trigger under automation.
- Layout: tree pane, body pane, status line; and whether panes are resizable.
- Editing: inline editor versus `$EDITOR` handoff. The second is simpler and reuses the author's
  editor; the first is faster for small bodies.
- How sync results and findings are presented, and whether the TUI can apply grammar findings.
- Whether the TUI requires an open book or can open one from a picker.


<a id="risks-and-constraints-14"></a>

### Risks and constraints

- A TUI that duplicates logic is the failure mode of this scope. It must be a view over the core.
- Hidden interactivity breaks automation. Any auto-detection of a TTY must be explicit and
  overridable.
- Terminal rendering differs between Windows and Unix; test the rendered lines, not the escape
  sequences.
- The TUI is the last phase. It must not block M5 or any earlier milestone.
